messages.author: Zhe
messages.text: The meeting room booking page is showing duplicate time slots today, but the display outside the room looks normal. Anyone else seeing this?

messages.text: Okay, I'll submit it tomorrow morning.

messages.text: Is it the same when you tap the old bookmark on mobile?

messages.author: Gu Xin
messages.text: Same. For now, search by name from the homepage; I'll add the replacement link later.

messages.text: Last night's "Fully restored" status page update went out too early. The Asia nodes still had two alerts at the time.

messages.author: He Jun
messages.text: Should we send the customer announcement again?

messages.author: Gao Yan
messages.text: No need to overwrite the old announcement; I've already appended the recovery time and affected areas to the original.

messages.author: Zhe
messages.text: Saw the update. The original link still works.

messages.author: Gao Yan
messages.text: Yes, the old page will keep the correction timestamp.

messages.author: Fu Ning
messages.text: This week's community open day still needs two volunteer guides; it won't take up time on the project schedule.

messages.author: Zheng Wei
messages.text: I can come for an hour. Let's DM about the exact time.

messages.author: Fu Ning
messages.text: That's enough, thanks. No need to report the remaining time in the group chat.

messages.author: Li Kai
messages.text: Thursday's Q&A for new hires has moved to the small meeting room on the third floor. The online link hasn't changed.

messages.author: Wang Zhenyu
messages.text: Will there be a recording? I'll be on a customer call then.

messages.author: Beibei
messages.text: Next Monday is holiday on-call duty; regular inquiries resume Tuesday.

messages.author: Sun Ting
messages.text: Do urgent escalations still go through the same channel?

messages.author: He Jun
messages.text: The desk temperature survey only collects floor and time slot, not names.

messages.author: Jiang Chuan
messages.text: Can the person on night duty fill it out too?

messages.author: He Jun
messages.text: Yes, just put "on duty" in the notes.

messages.author: Jiang Chuan
messages.text: Maintenance for shared execution pool 18:30; tasks already running won't be forcibly stopped.

messages.text: Do queued tasks count as already started?

messages.text: Doesn't count. I wasn't clear earlier: queued items will wait until maintenance is over.

messages.author: Han Mei
messages.text: Got it, won't resubmit manually.

messages.author: Bai
messages.text: The internal software list is missing two versions added after June. Don't uninstall anything based on it yet.

messages.author: Wang Zhenyu
messages.text: Is the page delayed, or did the scan not run at all?

messages.author: Bai
messages.text: The scan ran; the import job is stuck in the queue. The cause is still being investigated.

messages.author: Wang Zhenyu
messages.text: Then I'll mark this week's inventory as incomplete for now.

messages.author: Wang Zhenyu
messages.text: The old training portal will be archived at the end of the month; completion records will remain available for read-only lookup.

messages.text: Will incomplete courses be moved to the new portal automatically?

messages.text: It won't be moved automatically; the course owner decides whether to reopen it.

messages.author: Shen Jia

messages.author: Dong Yue
messages.text: I read a maintenance note about Micro QR's public interface and where ECC isn't supported. It separates observations from recommendations and even keeps the bookmark example as `MEBKM:TITLE:Example;URL:https\://example.test;;`. That's easier to read than just giving conclusions.

messages.author: Liu Chang
messages.text: Which versions did it sample? It's hard to compare the conclusions without the version range.

messages.author: Jiang Chuan
messages.text: Has anyone made a before-and-after chart showing capacity changes and finder stability for a regular QR? I'd like to see a very small example.

messages.author: Mia Chen
messages.text: Did that once. It looks pretty clear with a small input, but once the file gets long, everything gets crammed onto one line.

messages.author: Bai
messages.text: Then how about a small example each for `quiet zone` and `row stride`?

messages.author: Mia Chen
messages.text: Sure. This week I'm only showing small examples, not using it to assess large projects.

messages.text: I'll jot down what each of the two chart types hides.

messages.text: For this week's short talk, I'd like to cover pooled PNG raster fidelity, mainly looking at how to reduce failing samples step by step.

messages.text: Can you save an intermediate state from the reduction? The final sample often doesn't show what got dropped earlier.

messages.author: Zheng Wei
messages.text: Yes, three steps. The original input has already been replaced with a public example.

messages.author: He Jun
messages.text: Rereading the release notes for compressed QRCodeData round trips. The compatibility wording is a lot more conservative than the code examples.

messages.text: Are the instructions and examples from the same version?

messages.author: Beibei
messages.text: No, the example came one version later; I think that's the interesting part.

messages.author: Han Mei
messages.text: Just put the two dates side by side. No need to decide which one's right.

messages.author: Li Kai
messages.text: Anyone know a small public repo for practicing vCard 4 preferred work address? Ideally one that runs offline too.

messages.author: Dong Yue
messages.text: Just listened to a talk on reproducible builds and dependency provenance. The most useful part wasn't the conclusions—it was that they kept the hypotheses that had been disproved.

messages.author: Dong Yue
messages.text: Does the recording include the raw results, or are the slides all that's left?

messages.author: Gao Yan
messages.text: The appendix has results from two rounds. The second round crosses out the first round's attribution.

messages.author: Liu Chang
messages.text: This part is worth discussing on its own. We can skip the details of which tools were used.

messages.author: Dong Yue
messages.text: I'll pull out two sections of the timeline, not bring over the whole thing.

messages.author: Jiang Chuan
messages.text: I want to try a document-readability comparison: for error classification and what callers can see, only check whether a newcomer can reproduce it on their first attempt.

messages.author: Mia Chen
messages.text: Do participants need to be familiar with `public API` beforehand?

messages.author: Bai
messages.text: No. One group gets only a brief explanation, the other gets the full reference page.

messages.author: Xie An
messages.text: Found a little tool that can replay things commit by commit. Going to use it to see how the baseline, counterexamples, and rollback evidence have changed.

messages.text: Does it include generated files too?

messages.author: Zheng Wei
messages.text: It does by default; you have to exclude it manually. I haven't tried it on a large repo yet.

messages.author: Wang Zhenyu
messages.text: Then let's just look at the differences before and after filtering this week. We can talk about whether to adopt it later.

messages.author: He Jun
messages.text: Saw an interview about maintainers handing over responsibility for a legacy interface's compatibility window. It only listed three outstanding issues.

messages.author: Han Mei
messages.text: Was there any later mention of who took over?

messages.author: Li Kai

messages.author: Zhe
messages.text: Did you measure warm-up and dependency downloads separately?

messages.author: Sun Ting
messages.text: Haven't broken it down yet, so this week I'm only sharing the data collection method, no rankings.

messages.author: Beibei
messages.text: Anyone want to take a slow walk along the river this weekend? I'd like to pick a route where we can bail out at any point.

messages.text: Thinking of trying that noodle place for lunch. They don't take reservations; check the instructions in the attachment if you want to come.

messages.author: Dong Yue
messages.text: I'll head over a bit early and grab four seats.

messages.text: Could someone bring a small speaker along to the lawn? Just keep the volume low.

messages.text: I've got one. The battery will probably only last for half of it.

messages.text: I'll come at a different time than you.

messages.author: Gao Yan
